title: Descendents Of Lenepveu Threaten Legal Action Over Paris Opera Ceiling
summary: In 1962, Marc Chagall embarked on a secret commission from the French culture minister, André Malraux: 24 wedge-shaped canvases to be installed on the ceiling of Paris’s Palais Garnier opera house. summary: Prague is set to welcome its first international contemporary art fair next spring, with the launch of Prague Contemporary. The fair is the brainchild of founder and director Alexandra Karpuchina, the owner of Prague’s Karpuchina Gallery (formerly Black Pearl Gallery). title: Qing Dynasty Ceramics on Display at British Museum Found Damaged
summary: A three-hundred-year-old Jingdezhen porcelain bowl and box were found in shards inside a glass case at the British Museum after the bowl apparently tumbled from its shelf in the display. title: After Founder’s Untimely Death, New Owners for NYC’s Lubov Gallery
summary: New York gallery Lubov has announced Mode Bonafilia and Kristen Wasik as its new owners. The pair succeed gallery founder Francisco Correa Cordero, who died suddenly this past August at the age of thirty-seven. summary: Among the three centuries of work in the Philadelphia Museum of Art’s semiquincentennial exhibition “A Nation of Artists” is an eighty-three-pound alkaline-glazed stoneware jar made by the enslaved potter David Drake, also known as Dave the Potter, in 1859. title: Austrian Presidential Hopeful Vows To Repatriate Moctezuma’s Headdress To Mexico
summary: Gunther Fehlinger-Jahn, an Austrian economist, analyst, and 2028 presidential hopeful, has declared his intent to return a 16th-century feather headdress to Mexico if he is elected. summary: A pair of paintings by Pierre-Auguste Renoir that were stolen last month from the artist’s namesake museum in Cagnes-sur-Mer, France, were found by local officials.
